data.why: The repo ships two runnable example packages; the web app's sidebar has a text field for a server-local package path (resolved against the server's working directory, /work/app), so typing 'examples/full_presubmission_package' or 'examples/minimal_package' runs the audit without needing a file upload.

goals: Run a first-pass pre-submission self-audit on a manuscript package and read the Quick Read / Must Resolve / Materials Needed summary
Check whether declared figure-to-raw-image and figure-to-source-data traceability links hold up, and see any manifest_conflict flags
Review the claim-to-evidence coverage table built from claim_manifest.csv to find claims lacking source data, raw records, or analysis code
Inspect flagged statistical patterns (SD/SEM/n consistency, p-value ranges, Benford-style digit prompts) and decide which need author explanation
Use the image-review packet / external-tool handoff list to triage candidate duplicate or spliced figure panels
Compare two audit runs (before/after fixing gaps) with the re-audit diff view to confirm findings were resolved

review.summary: The tree is honest, well evidenced for what it reached, and accurately maps the documentation side of the tool: package prep, run modes, coverage, action tracking and the re-audit diff, with mostly clean general and specific labels. Because both demo packages were clean, it never shows the tool's core job of surfacing and triaging candidate image, statistical and manifest-conflict findings, so it needs a second pass on a seeded package before filing.
